# Anthony Tulk

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
- **Role:** pupil  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Anthony has a small, dark, and gloomy face with black eyes. His appearance suggests he could be a fairly pleasant boy if his sullen exterior were ever penetrated.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004), [v2 c5 P10](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0010)_

## Personality

Anthony is a sullen, cheeky, and disdainful boy who behaves with an impertinent swagger. He displays hostility and glaring enmity toward his teacher, Nell, resisting her efforts to win his favor and listening to her lectures with contempt. Though defiant and prone to looking at others without shame or embarrassment, he is clever and possesses deep emotions, venting his distress through deliberate fights.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004), [v2 c5 P10](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0010), [v2 c7 P5](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0005), [v2 c12 P1](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0001), [v2 c12 P28](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0028), [v2 c26 P34](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0034)_

## History

Anthony Tulk, an orphaned nephew of Timothy Cotton, was taken in by Mrs. Laurence Tulk and enrolled as a student in Nell Harcourt's schoolroom. From the beginning, Anthony displayed enmity toward Nell, glaring at her sullenly and defying her efforts to win his affection. On one occasion, he poured the contents of his slate bottle down Aurelia Clay's neck and left his reprimand with a contemptuous whistle. Despite his disdainful attitude, Nell recognized him as a clever boy, though his noncompliance negatively influenced the rest of the class. During a particularly tense day at school, Anthony swaggered into the cold classroom, made impertinent remarks, and was eventually punished with a pointer until his defiance gave way to tears. However, when news arrived that Nell had resigned, Anthony vented his true distress over her departure by engaging in two deliberate, unprovoked fights with other boys.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P4](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0004), [v2 c5 P10](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0010), [v2 c7 P5](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0005), [v2 c12 P1](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0001), [v2 c12 P33](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0033), [v2 c26 P34](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0034)_
